content:
maria: Quick q — thinking about pushing `deadline_hint` handling into the enqueue fastpath instead of letting the queue broker annotate. Pros/cons?
saul: I like the idea for latency predictability — fewer hops to consult when scheduling. :thumbsup:
jin: main risk is duplication of logic across producers, + harder to change semantics later. If we bake it in fastpath we need a single lib used by SDK + internal callers.
dave: can you sketch the fastpath flow? where would kv-cache pinning interact?
maria: sketch: 
```
producer -> admission_fastpath { attach deadline_hint; accounting } -> queue_broker -> scheduler
```
broker currently infers deadlines from route/model + payload size. fastpath would compute a deadline score and attach a small 8b field.
saul: that 8b field is good. keep it opaque number score, not absolute timestamp. broker can still override if it thinks differently.
jin: override behavior is key — if broker overrides we need a safe merge rule. i propose: `min(producer_score, broker_score)` where lower means tighter deadline. simple and monotonic.
maria: agreed. also we should keep a provenance bitmask: bit0=producer, bit1=broker so we know who contributed. helps debugging.
dave: what about prefetch/prefill? if producer attaches tight deadline but prefetch already started, we might starve prefetch or cause wasted work.
saul: we can add a `prefetch_conservative` flag computed at admission: if payload.is_prefetch then bump score by +1 (looser).
jin: question on telemetry: we need histograms for score at each boundary (producer, broker, selected). add tags: origin=producer|broker.
ops-bot: deploy-note: scheduler-service-v2 will roll 7/12 -> watch batch_latency SLA.
maria: migration plan: 1) implement helper lib in infra/sdk 2) prod callers opt-in for 2 weeks 3) enable default attach in edge nodes 4) broker read-only mode for 1 week 5) broker enforcement on.
dave: opt-in knob should be per-tenant so we can test on dedicated pools. also need a feature flag to revert.
saul: concurrency concern: if fastpath computes score we must keep it cheap — avoid any blocking IO. pure CPU math. keep it inlined.
jin: sample pseudo-code for score (very rough):
```
score = base_for_model(model_id)
score += log2(sequence_len)
if has_function_call then score -= 2
if is_system_prompt_heavy then score -= 1
```
lower -> more urgent.
maria: good. we'll also expose `score_reason` short enum for tracing.
dave: how does this change admission accounting? we still need tenant credits & headroom. score only influences scheduling priority. accounting unchanged.
saul: one more: KV cache pinning wants stronger affinity for urgent requests. broker decides placement; but if producer tight score, broker should prefer node with warm cache. we need an extra hint field `cache_affinity` boolean.
jin: keep it optional. broker can ignore it. but if present, scheduler picks nodes with warm entries first.
maria: next steps: i'll draft a tiny RFC with state machine, fields: `score:uint8`, `provenance:uint8`, `cache_affinity:bool`, `prefetch_flag:bool`. ping @jin @saul for review by EOD Friday.
saul: sounds good. also add backwards compatibility note: older clients without `score` default to broker-only path.
jin: and add test plan: unit tests for merge rule, property tests for monotonicity, canary on 5% traffic.
maria: thanks — i'll post RFC link when done. :sparkles:
